why: Owner's instruction: the spec can be published, so being unpublished is not a reason to drop it; use it only if it measurably helps. Supersedes D-004. Rule in docs/rules.md.

why: Owner's instruction. Held-out rule and data rule in docs/rules.md; training on Colab Pro, evaluation in the official harness.

title: Personaxis is rejected under the D-007 rule
why: Net = (2-4) at L0 + (3-7) at L2 = -6 <= -5 (C-018, C-023, C-031). pax is not used in the leaderboard bundle or in later waves; the paper reports the counts and the rule's outcome, and states that neither paired test is significant alone and that two arms of equal solve rate already differ on 27 tasks (C-027), so the result is 'no benefit found', not evidence of harm.

title: Failure labels are two axes fixed after reading wave-1 traces: patch state at grading (8 labels) and how the episode ended
why: The plan's single list mixed outcome and cause. Traces show the budget is rarely the primary cause at L3 and that two modes the list lacked dominate: output cut off at the token limit inside an edit call, and write_file overwriting an existing file with a truncated copy after edit_file rejections. Scheme and precedence in docs/rules.md; implemented by the work plan. Clipped-hint episodes get their own label and are excluded from shares.

title: Wave 2 tests the edit primitive at L3 (patch_L3) and measures the run-to-run flip rate (base_r2_L3, base_r2_L0)
why: 1 - Solve(L3) is the largest loss (C-022, C-026) and collapses with patch size (C-028). lean already removes write_file and tells the model to copy old_string exactly, yet lean_L3 equals base_L3 (C-027): instructions do not fix it, so the mechanism is changed instead. The patch bundle removes edit_file/write_file and applies one unified diff with git apply (atomic, no old/new string pairing). Reruns are needed because single-run pairs disagree on 27 tasks at equal rate. Skill scripts were not used: they depend on a code executor the scorer may not provide. patch at L0/L2 is not run: without the diff given it measures diff authoring, a different question, and quota is short. Localization aid, E4B and LoRA go to the work plan.

title: Title: Handed the Fix, Still Failing: An Oracle Ladder for Locating Where a 2.3B Agent Loses Software-Engineering Tasks
why: Given the reference diff the agent still fails 59.1% of tasks (C-022; 56.3% on complete hints, C-026), more than the localization gap (C-020) and the synthesis gap (C-021). The title states only this wave-1 result, so wave 2 cannot falsify it; 'surgical tools' moves to the discussion and is asserted only if patch_L3 beats base_L3 beyond the measured flip rate.

title: Leaderboard submission lb02 uses the lean bundle
why: At L0 base, lean and nothink are indistinguishable on the public tasks (C-001, C-006, C-008, C-015, C-017) and pax is rejected. lb01 already scored base; submitting lean buys a second hidden-set data point at the same expected score and a shorter median episode. title: Last day of the Paper Track: build and test the hunk edit protocol (wave 3) with rules fixed before the data; the submitted Writeup stays valid until a verified replacement exists
why: Owner review 2026-11-11: the Writeup diagnoses but nothing in it works better. Judgement: strong on verifiability and clarity, moderate on novelty, weak on impact, one model only. A gain in the competition condition cannot be shown in a day: base solves 8/127 at L0 and identical runs flip 6 tasks (C-046). L3 has the power, and the wave-2 traces name what to fix in the patch channel: 73 corrupt-count rejections, 48 context mismatches, 44 token-limit cut-offs, atomic failure (C-054..C-056). The harness is declarative only, so the guards and line-addressed edits of the Discussion cannot be built as tools; git apply flags can do per-hunk apply and tolerant matching inside the bundle (--recount --reject --unidiff-zero --ignore-whitespace, one file per command, max_output_tokens 16384). The D-011 rule compared a net margin with a gross count (about 4.6 standard deviations between identical runs); wave 3 uses an exact sign-flip test over two treatment and two control runs at p < 0.01, and reports the D-011 outcome beside it. Carry-over to L2 and L0 is predicted to be absent and tested. LoRA cannot be trained, validated and evaluated in 28 h without risking the rest; it stays in the work plan. Design in docs/rules.md, packages the work plan and the work plan.

title: hunk bundle uses max_output_tokens 8192, not 16384
why: Owner delegated the call to execution (2026-11-11 ~21:00Z). wave3_smoke: 2/6 episodes ended with ContextWindowExceededError (I-011). From traces: with 16384 every prompt above 16384 tokens fails; wave1 base_L3 had 12/127 such episodes, base_L0 16/127, wave2 base_r2_L3 4/127, so hunk would be handicapped exactly where controls are not. With 8192 the prompt limit is 24576: 0 of 1651 earlier episodes reached it (max 23158). Completions at the 8192 cap are rare at L3 (7-9 of ~1000 steps per arm) and degenerate; the one smoke completion that reached 16384 consumed the context and caused a failure. 8192 also makes hunk differ from base and patch only in the edit protocol. Smoke not rerun: 8192 is the setting of 1651 graded episodes and the acceptance checks concern the git apply command, unaffected.

title: Paper is rewritten around the carry-over result; wave 4 (E4B at L0 and L2) uses the remaining quota; no competition-condition improvement is claimed
why: Owner objection 2026-11-12: neither paper-v1 nor the hunk rewrite shows a contribution, because hunk helps only when the fix is handed over. Verdict: the objection is right on the facts. Nothing in this project raises the solve rate at L0, and nothing that could has evidence behind it and fits in one 2.3 h run: file names (L1) and hidden tests (T) give E2B nothing, hunk gives nothing at L0, a LoRA is not trained, and passing p < 0.01 at L0 needs about +14 tasks on 8. The rewrite is still chosen over keeping paper-v1, for correctness rather than impact: paper-v1 tells builders the edit path is the first thing to work on, and wave 3 refutes that (rule iii met at L3, C-064; no carry-over at L2 or L0 and every difference against the protocol, C-070, C-071). The new text says in the abstract and the limitations that nothing here raises the competition score, reports the L3 gain as a transfer result only, notes that the first hunk run equals patch (C-099), and makes the claim: the largest oracle residual was not the bottleneck; what binds is the content of the change. Claims C-060..C-095 recomputed from results.jsonl and by rerunning the tools (outputs byte-identical): all verified; C-096..C-099 added. Rules applied: (iii) met; (iv) no effect claimed at L2 or L0, as predicted, with the sign noted; the D-011 rule is met by hunk_r2_L3 only. Wave 4: base_e4b at L0 and L2 (runs/_configs/wave4.json, deadline_minutes 100, drop base_e4b_L2 if less than 4.0 h of quota is left). It is the only use of the last quota that serves both the paper (second model had L3 only) and December (dev-set number for an E4B bundle). Its two solve counts enter the paper through one fixed sentence that execution fills in; execution may set those two claims verified only if all 127 rows of the arm have status done and a recount of results.jsonl equals analysis.json. If wave 4 is not analysed by 09:00 UTC the paper goes without it. Expected standing, stated to the owner: strong on verifiability and clarity, a real but modest insight, weak on impact; a top-3 place is unlikely against entries that report working gains.

title: The old pax arm was an incomplete application of Personaxis; pax2 rebuilds it to the spec and is tested once on E4B at L0 (wave 5) with a rule fixed now
why: Owner (creator of the Personaxis spec), 2026-11-12: the pax bundle of wave 1 did not apply the spec properly. Audit: it compiled personaxis.md to a prompt with the PERSONA_template headings (prompts/system.md) but omitted personality, affect, cognition and metacognition, had no knowledge/, no creation report, and put the definition under persona/. pax2 (agents/pax2, agents/pax2_e4b): personaxis.md with the ten layers (validates against persona.schema.json), PERSONA.md compiled by hand to PERSONA_template.md (CLI not installed) and read as the instruction, skill repair-a-reported-defect with its guarantee, six sourced knowledge topics in knowledge/ exposed through a knowledge skill (the harness only lets the agent reach files through skills), creation-report.md. No Personaxis runtime exists in the harness: the guarantee's checks are answered by the agent with one git diff command. Rule, fixed before any pax2 data: pax2_e4b_L0 (wave 5) vs base_e4b_L0 (wave 4, 18/127), paired on 127 tasks; the persona is said to raise the solve rate iff exact McNemar p < 0.01 with more tasks only pax2; to lower it iff p < 0.01 the other way; otherwise 'not shown', reported with its counts. One run each side; same machine shape (Kaggle 4x L4), same harness, tools, sampling and budget. Old pax claims (C-009, C-010, C-018, C-019, C-023, C-031) are to be marked as a test of an incomplete application, not of the format. Owner delegated execution to execution in chat; Colab port is the route for further runs when Kaggle quota is out.

title: pax3: Personaxis 2.1.0 compile with the procedure and knowledge inline in PERSONA.md; tested 2 vs 2 on Colab with a sign-flip rule fixed now
why: Owner (2026-11-12 ~08:45Z): audit and improve the persona implementation, any experiment allowed on the Colab GPU. Audit of pax2 (C-105..C-111): the skill was loaded in ~80% of episodes and knowledge almost never; versus base on the same A100 the first edit came at median call 6 instead of 4, read_file 775 vs 578, search_similar_code 40 vs 101, 12 vs 7 timeouts, 110 vs 124 submits. Hypothesis: loading costs calls and time in a 24-call, 5-minute budget, and a 4B model does not fetch knowledge on its own; a runtime would place it in context. pax3 = pax2's definition (ten layers, schema-valid) compiled so that PERSONA.md carries the skill's steps and the knowledge practices inline, no skill loading; two practices are taken from the official starter prompt (search_similar_code before grep, docs_src). Designed after reading traces of the same 127 public tasks: not a held-out test, and the paper must say so if it reports it. Rule fixed now, before any pax3 data: runs cb_pax3_e4b_L0 and cb_pax3_r2_e4b_L0 (colab_e4b_L0_r2) against cb_base_e4b_L0 (colab_e4b_L0) and cb_base_r2_e4b_L0 (colab_e4b_L0_r2), all on one A100; per task d = pax3 solves - base solves, exact two-sided sign-flip test; the persona raises the solve rate iff D > 0 and p < 0.01; otherwise not shown. Each pax3 vs base pairing is reported with exact McNemar p.

title: Round 1: per-task budget (15 min, 60 calls) and the Personaxis 2.1 work-acceptance gate (paxgate), E4B at L0 on two Colab A100s

Rules fixed before any data: (a) paxgate vs base15, exact McNemar: shown iff p < 0.01 with more tasks only paxgate; (b) budget: base15 vs each of the two 5-minute Colab base runs (colab_e4b_L0, colab_e4b_L0_r2): shown iff p < 0.01 in both, same sign. title: Round 3: paxreview and regguard, two runs each, confirmatory tests fixed now
why: Round 2 learning: with its path fixed the gate runs (check written in ~105/127 episodes) but the 4B model makes its own check pass in only ~9% of episodes, and a passing check predicts the hidden tests in 36%. Next, two mechanisms that do not need the model to write a correct test: paxreview (Personaxis review by an independent model step over the diff, then one revision) and regguard (run the repository's existing tests of the changed module before submitting). Fixed before any data: for each, exact sign-flip test of its two runs (colab_r3a, colab_r3b) against the two base15 runs (colab_r1a, colab_r2b); shown iff D > 0 and p < 0.01. Two tests are run; neither is claimed at p >= 0.01.

title: Round 4: independent replication of paxreview (fresh runs only); think15 and temp06 are dropped
why: Round 3: paxreview x2 (21, 19) vs base15 x2 (14, 12) passed D-032 (D +14, p 0.0061), but (1) two tests ran in that round and many variants ran today, so 0.0061 would not survive a Bonferroni split of 0.01 over two tests; (2) the two base15 runs are among the lowest base runs (the 5-minute base runs gave 19 and 17). Fixed now, before any round-4 data, to decide whether the paper may report the review step as an improvement: replication test = exact sign-flip test of the two NEW paxreview runs (cb_paxreview_r3_e4b_L0 in colab_r4a, cb_paxreview_r4_e4b_L0 in colab_r4b) against the two NEW base15 runs in the same campaigns (cb_base15_r3_e4b_L0, cb_base15_r4_e4b_L0); replicated iff D > 0 and p < 0.01. Reported beside it, not deciding: the pooled 4 vs 4 test over rounds 3 and 4. If not replicated, the paper reports the review step as not shown. Deadline cut-off D-029 applies: if round 4 is not complete by about 20:45 UTC it is not used.

title: Paper without Personaxis: the review step did not replicate
why: D-033 replication failed (C-138: D -1, p 1); pooled 4 vs 4 p 0.072 (C-139). Following the owner's instruction (Personaxis in the paper only if positive) and the pre-registered rules, the Writeup carries no Personaxis result. The failed replication of a p = 0.006 pass is the strongest evidence yet for the paper's evaluation advice (rerun, fix the rule first), so one generic sentence reports it without naming the method.
